recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is; no core FHIR follow-up is needed unless a future work group decision changes the UDI carrier encoding or entry-type model.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification Device issue requesting clarified AIDC support guidance for Device.udiCarrier, including support where AIDC can be distinguished from user-entered UDI carrier data.
initial_application: The 2017 Device UDI commit series 2bd8c95642d3, 05a8652714ff, and d9163a93a7ba explicitly cited [11049] and [11050], split UDI carrier representation into HRF and AIDC forms, and added entry-type examples/source support.
additional_context: Device is active in source/fhir.ini. Current Device.udiCarrier.carrierAIDC is base64Binary and its definition explains that AIDC representations may include non-printable characters and therefore SHALL be base64Binary encoded; carrierHRF separately carries the human-readable form. FHIR-11050 supplies the entryType mechanism that differentiates capture methods. Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting later community decision.
reconciliation: No source change was made because the current build inputs already support AIDC carrier conveyance and capture-method differentiation.

related_jiras.note: Requested the entryType mechanism used to distinguish user-entered from machine-read AIDC UDI carrier data.
